title: Write visibility by shape — sequential, parallel, and after a join
proves: An edge orders a write against what runs after it: a node reading its immediate predecessor's key always sees it, and a node after a Wait for All sees every joined branch's key. Two PARALLEL branches are deliberately not asserted — there is no happens-before between them, which is what Wait for All exists to provide.
notes:
Companion to loop-write-visibility, mapping WHICH shapes are ordered. Measured unpatched vs patched in fractal-core, 300 runs each:
  back-to-back (a1 -> a2)      1/300 missed the write  ->  0/300 after the fix
  after Wait for All (c1,c2)   0/300 both arms          ->  the join was already a correct barrier
  parallel cross-read (b1,b2)  ~7-12% missed, BOTH arms ->  unchanged, and correct

`b1_saw_b2` and `b2_saw_b1` are recorded but NOT asserted on purpose. Two branches off Start have no ordering between them, so either value is legitimate; asserting on them would encode a guarantee the engine does not make, and 'fixing' it would mean synchronising every write to hide a real design constraint. If you want one branch to see another's work, join them.

Needs no model, no plugin, no network and no secret — js, rule and promissall only.
